classificationDecisions: The section-3 and review-section parent shall governs the content list. Separate exact parent and child spans are disclosed as noncontiguous quotations; intervening list text is not silently presented as consecutive prose.

Engineering artifacts, requirements, analyses and processes named in the list are required presentation information for the contract-required review scope. These records do not independently require execution of every engineering task or review.

Section 3.11 explicitly states that Content Definitions shall contain the following. Its 26 definition items are therefore retained as definition-content records with the Content Definitions section as actor, rather than converting descriptive engineering processes into execution obligations.
The embedded Design Reference Mission shall in 3.2.u is retained as the package's information about intended DRM use, not as a separate engineering-execution requirement.

The final must in 3.11.s directs engineering allocation of end-item quantitative requirements; no separate engineering-execution record is extracted. The Allocation Report definition's methods and results remain required definition content.
The should clauses in 3.11.v and 3.11.x do not become mandatory execution instructions. Records cover the explicitly required definitions of plan content only.
Conditional architecture layers in 3.4.h, 3.5.gg and 3.6.gg retain the condition that layers have been defined. PRR content preserves the no-less-than minimum-list meaning.
Source typographical defects are preserved in quotations. In particular, 3.11.w repeats tasks and ends with the incomplete phrase from the; no missing continuation is invented.
Named source categories and government organizations are source content, not fabricated program examples. No program, contractor, employer or contract-number sample was added.
coverage.granularity: One record per coherent obligation: 2 common rules, 1 package section-structure rule, 1 review-content coverage rule and 26 distinct definition-content duties. No repeated product/review obligation records. The C reference table carries all 328 native review-content entries in 256 exact-label rows across 10 review columns, plus 26 coherent definitions; exact qualifiers and conditions remain.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: This instruction applies to all NAVAIR, which includes NAVAIR Headquarters, Competencies, Program Executive Officers (PEOs), Program Managers AIR (PMA), subordinate commands and field activities involved with the design, development, test and evaluation (T&E), acquisition, in-service support, and disposal of Naval aviation systems and equipment. For Joint programs with Navy as the lead service, this instruction applies, but may be amended to accommodate partner interests.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Scope of the provided issue; not a present-day universal rule for all contractors. Current status remains unverified.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: Reference (a) provides guidance related to SETR checklists, checklist tailoring and checklist completion. SETR checklists include entry criteria for each review, as delineated in enclosure (2).
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Links the appropriate checklist to enclosure (2); read with the operative duties in 5e and 5f. This is supporting declarative context, not a separately manufactured shall.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: As such, the SEP does not contain language directing contractors to accomplish specific work in a contractually binding environment. Therefore, elements of the SEP and this instruction should be translated into the Statement of Work (SOW) and established in Contract Data Requirements Lists (CDRLs) to support the execution of the SETR process and events. As a standalone citation within the RFP, the SEP and this instruction only provides background information of NAVAIR applicable processes and can be useful guidance for the development of the contractor System Engineering Management Plan (SEMP).
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Express limit on inferring contractor obligations. The should-language is not promoted to an independent shall; no current referenced instruction is substituted.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: Tailoring takes the form of deletion (removal of reviews and elements not applicable), alteration (modifying and combining reviews and elements to more explicitly reflect the application to a particular effort) or addition (adding reviews and elements to satisfy program requirements). Tailoring shall be performed in breadth and depth of SETR process as applied to any particular program. Tailoring in breadth defines the number and type of SETR events and audits. Tailoring in depth defines the activity and elements associated with individual SETR or audit events, which is frequently accomplished by tailoring the SETR checklist and tailoring the substantiating evidence required to demonstrate design maturity and contractual compliance.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: This paragraph controls tailoring scope; the conduct of tailoring is not separately converted into a review-row data rule. The actual documentation obligation is separately extracted from 5c on page 7.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: SETR tailoring, to include SETR and audit events with entry criteria and required documentation shall be documented in the program's SEP and per reference (c) requirements.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Operative parent for documenting program-specific tailored review events, criteria, and required documentation.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: The tailored SETR events and audits shall be conducted per the approved program SEP on all programs. Smaller programs that may not have a program SEP are not exempt from the policy of conducting SETR events, or tailoring SETR events according to size, risk and complexity of the program.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Conduct duty retained as scope context; not converted into a mandatory delivered checklist row or a mandate to conduct every event in the standard list.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: The Systems Engineer shall be responsible for assessing the status of SETR entry criteria. Each SETR event has a set of associated SETR Entry Criteria per enclosure (2). An assessment of entry criteria is used to judge program readiness and maturity to proceed with the SETR event.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Operative assessment parent. This supports assessing the applicable enclosure criteria, not a claim that every criterion is already met or requires an individual deliverable.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: The Systems Engineer shall be responsible for tailoring and completing the appropriate SETR Checklist.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Operative checklist tailoring/completion parent; no native data encoding or scoring equation is specified.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: The tailoring of the SETR Checklist shall be approved by the designated TRB Chair.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Operative approval duty; does not specify a signature format or machine-readable approval field.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: The Systems Engineer is responsible for providing the final assessment to the TRB Chair, TRB members and designated competency representatives prior to the review. Based on the completed SETR Checklist, the TRB Chair determines readiness to conduct the SETR event.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Nonmodal source context for assessment recipients/timing and readiness decision. Not extracted as a new literal shall/must/prohibition. No universal all-pass or numeric threshold is provided.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: The products resulting from a SETR event include independent capability assessment, technical baseline assessment, risk assessments, risk mitigation options, NAVAIR 4355/4 (Rev. 10/2014), Request for Action (RFA) forms, SETR minutes and the TRB Chair Report. The SETR event produces a TRB Chair Report based on an integrated technical (e.g., logistics, engineering, T&E) assessment of the system in development.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Product inventory and report basis are declarative context, not a separate new modal mandate. Body does not provide native schemas for these products.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: Key products of the review include the SETR checklist, NAVAIR 4355/4 and TRB Chair Closure Memo.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Declarative product inventory. Closure memo content, exit criteria, and form fields are not supplied by this body statement.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: Support the PMA to ensure each program has a SEP and ensure the SETR process, including SETR event, are adequately addressed in that plan and related contract(s).
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Inherited 6f modal governs a broader planning/contract responsibility. Catalogued here rather than extracted as additional F7 review-record rows; do not recast as direct contractor commitment.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: Ensure consistency between the System Design Specification, SEP, CMP, SOW and other RFP documentation with the delivered contractor documentation (SEMP, CMP, etc.).
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Inherited 6f modal governs cross-document consistency across other feeds. Catalogued context only, with no new contractor or field-level requirement.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: Records created as a result of this instruction, regardless of media and format, shall be managed per SECNAV Manual 5210.1, Department of the Navy Records Management Manual.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Operative records-management dependency; uninspected referenced manual supplies no extracted retention, disposition, or media constraints here.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: The reporting requirements contained in paragraph 4a(5) are exempt from reports controlled per SECNAV Manual 5214.1, part IV, paragraph 7k.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Report-control exemption is limited to the cited paragraph and manual provision; not an exemption from making or retaining the underlying review records.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: NAVAIR 4355/4 (Rev. 10/2014), Request for Action Form can be downloaded from Navy Forms Online at https://navalforms.documentservices.dla.mil/web/public/home
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Identifies the form/version referenced by this issue. The form was not provided or opened; its field layout is unknown here.

scopeAndFieldFacts.passage: SETRs are considered complete when all RFAs are signed off, and an acceptable level of program risk is ascertained. The SETRs are formally completed by the TRB Chairperson via a letter of closure.
scopeAndFieldFacts.effect: Completion definition directly read and visually verified from the provided PDF. Retained as source context rather than manufactured into a new literal shall/must/prohibition record. The acceptable-risk threshold is not quantified. This is not an event-by-event exit-criteria table or a numeric readiness formula.
